regulator: No dedicated waterway transit authority — all services are tour/charter. Marinha do Brasil (Capitania dos Portos, Angra dos Reis delegacia) certifies vessels/crews; ANTAQ regulates waterway passenger services; Prefeitura de Paraty licenses tour boats and manages the Cais de Turismo; ICMBio (APA Cairuçu) and INEA (Reserva Ecológica da Juatinga) govern the protected waters; the site is managed under the UNESCO 'Paraty and Ilha Grande' mixed World Heritage inscription (2019).
annual_basis_note: DISPLAY-ONLY market: no regulated/official waterway passenger series exists for Paraty (no scheduled public ferry; the CCR Barcas system does not serve Paraty). The 3.5M/yr figure is total destination visitation (municipal estimate via mayoral interview), not boardings; waterway volume can only be inferred qualitatively from the ~50-schooner fleet (avg ~150 pax capacity) sailing daily. FX converted at 5.0727 BRL/USD (BCB PTAX 2026-07-15).
gaps: No official annual waterway/boarding passenger series — Prefeitura/Capitania do not publish Cais de Turismo boarding counts; request from Secretaria de Turismo de Paraty for any economics work.
3.5M visitors/yr is a mayoral-interview estimate, not an audited series; an older academic estimate (2003) was ~232k tourists/yr — the methodology gap between the two is unresolved.
Schooner fleet count (~50, Associação das Escunas via Valor) covers Paraty-based escunas only; total licensed lancha/charter fleet size not found in an official register.

No premium ride-hail comparable: Uber/99 have no reliable availability in Paraty (local taxi/mototáxi only) — road comparable would be private transfer pricing (e.g., Paraty↔GRU airport transfers), not ride-hail.
Paraty Mirim and Trindade landing operations (exact ops point, any municipal fees) unverified beyond OSM geometry and tour-operator pages.
